summary: Shadowed prefix writes creating lookup locks and serialized KV reads causing p99 latency on repeated prompts
description:
Issue summary:
Customer VerityAI reported sudden p99 latency increases (400-600ms extra) on repeated identical prompts in a conversational flow. Problem first observed 2026-03-12 15:22 UTC. Requests that previously hit prefix/KV cache are observed to stall and fall back to cold KV reads or serialized shard reads leading to timeouts in some streaming sessions.

Impact:
- Several production API calls for a major customer (dedicated capacity) experienced p99 token latency increases from ~60ms to ~450-700ms for identical prompt retriggers.
- Some streaming connections dropped (client observed truncated streams) when tail latency crossed streaming heartbeat window.
- Customer throughput reduced, perceived as a regression in model responsiveness.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool id: dp-verit-3 (us-east)
- Serving runtime: rti-v2.4.7
- KV-store: kv-shardset-v8 (internal) with per-shard locking for prefix namespace
- Model: redwood/gptj-13b-q4 pinned to v2026-03-10

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) POST identical prompt A -> expecting cached prefix hit and low latency.
2) Repeat prompt A 20x at ~20 qps (same session id) -> observe intermittent p99 spikes and occasional 504 on stream reconnects.

Logs / traces attached in linked PR and Observability snapshots. Notable traces show: 
- First request in burst: cache miss -> backend read (~30ms)
- Subsequent identical requests: cache state set to "shadowing" for prefix shard -> lock acquired, requests serialized on shard lock causing queued KV read latencies 200-600ms
- Fallback path triggers cold read and runtime re-fetch causing additional token emission delay.

Observations:
- The prefix/kvcache state machine has a new code path that marks a prefix as "shadowing" during concurrent write/rehash. While shadowing, lookups that arrive attempt to acquire a shard-level exclusive lock instead of optimistic read path.
- This reproduces only on high-concurrency identical-prefix bursts (common in repeat prompt/bot loops).
- Correlated increased number of "acquire_lock" events in metrics around 2026-03-12 15:20 UTC for dp-verit-3.

Hypothesis:
- A recent change (PR #4281) introduced stronger serialization during prefix write/rehash to avoid stale index reads, but it did not gate optimistic concurrent read path. Under high identical-prefix concurrency this causes lock contention and serialized KV reads, multiplying p99 latency.

Immediate customer-facing mitigation suggested:
- Temporarily route VerityAI traffic to alternate dedicated pool (dp-verit-4) where the rehash rollout is not active.
- Apply temporary gateway rule to reduce per-session qps bursts (rate-limit smoothing) as a stopgap.

Required next steps:
- Engineering to triage PR #4281 and produce a hotfix that allows optimistic reads to proceed during shadowing or implements fine-grained per-prefix locks instead of coarse shard-level exclusive locks.
- Add observability alert for sudden increase in shard_lock_waits and "shadowing" state transitions.
- Run synthetic load reproducer against dp-verit-3 to validate fix.

Attachments:
- observability snapshot: /dashboards/trace/obs-20260312-dp-verit-3
- trace sample ids: trace-7a9c, trace-7a9d, trace-7a9f
- linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4281 (suspect change)

resolution_notes: 2026-03-14 14:30 - Hotfix merged to main: optimistic-read fast-path restored for prefix shadowing states (partial revert of exclusive lock semantics from PR 4281).
2026-03-14 15:00 - Hotfix rolled to dp-verit-3 in canary mode; preliminary metrics show p99 latency for repeat prompts returned to baseline (70ms -> 85ms).
Post-rollback actions: full rollout schedule, additional unit tests for prefix lifecycle, and an observability alert added for prefix_shadowing_count > threshold.
